title: HW↔QA-001: DFT Access & Test Fixtures + Coverage/HIL Requirements
description: The Hardware Engineer provides test points and DFT (Design for Test) access, test fixtures, manufacturing/test procedures, and reliability-test support; the QA & Test Automation Engineer provides test-coverage requirements, HIL (Hardware-in-the-Loop) test needs, and validation/defect findings from board testing. Grounded in HARDWARE_ENGINEER_SKILL §6.5 and QA_TEST_AUTOMATION_ENGINEER_SKILL §6.6.

hardware_test_enablement.description: HW→QA: test points / DFT access, fixtures, procedures, reliability-test support.

qa_test_requirements.description: QA→HW: coverage requirements, HIL needs, validation/defect findings.

x-macp.tier_rationale: Routine DFT-access / fixture handoff and board-test coordination is agent-autonomous (DFT planning; fixture handoff; reliability and environmental test campaigns). Defect findings flow into the QA go/no-go gate, which remains the permanent HITL stage-transition control.
x-macp.cadence: TRIGGER (DFT planning; fixture handoff; reliability and environmental test campaigns)
confirm_conditions: DFT access and test fixtures are provided against QA's coverage requirements
HIL test needs are addressed by the hardware test enablement
defect findings carry an id and a severity
reliability-test support is identified for the environmental campaign
reject_conditions: a board-test defect downgraded or omitted to clear a gate (Honesty Over Polish §10.3)
PRODUCTION test procedures asserted without the DFT access they depend on
a CRITICAL board-test defect presented as non-blocking for the QA go/no-go gate
counter_conditions: a coverage requirement has no corresponding test point / DFT access — request the access or a fixture before committing coverage
a HIL need exceeds available fixtures — request a fixture-development plan before the campaign
